text:
sara_morris: quick heads-up — after the q4b-int8 bring-up on dedicated, our canary 'goldlet' (small, high-signal promptset) shows a measurable quality regression on longcode and multi-turn stateful flows. :frowning:
jia_chen: ugh, saw the perf numbers earlier. is this the int8-only kernel or packing change?
marc_d: initial diffs point to tokenization + ordering for code prompts. some answers drop trailing context.
leila_ops: tagging infra — any recent runtime flags flipped during deploy? @tom_runtime
tom_runtime: deploy-bot shows a config change at 1759876000: `ENABLE_KV_COMPACT=true` + kernel swap to q4b-int8-v2. revertable if needed.
sara_morris: can we isolate: rerun the canary eval with the previous kernel (q4b-int8-v1) and with only the kernel swap (no compact) so we know which axis causes the regression?
marc_d: i can run a targeted evaltable. will need the canary prompt bundle (the goldlet) and the new model artifacts.
jia_chen: labelers already flagged 12/120 examples as "meaningfully different" in the quick audit. most are long code completions and follow-up corrections.
labelbot: NOTE: 12 examples flagged by QA-team. Link: https://redwood.infra/evals/1759/goldlet-audit
leila_ops: re: labeler capacity — current queue + priority: we have 48 label tasks free if we edge-prioritize this. want me to reassign?
sara_morris: yes please shift 30 labelers to high-priority micro-gold triage for the next 6h. we need clear diff annotations (regression vs acceptable formatting).
marc_d: executing evals now, two runs: baseline (q4b-int8-v1) and candidate (q4b-int8-v2 + kv_compact). ETA ~8m.
tom_runtime: started a canary replay job: job_id=canary-replay-1759876420. watching system traces.
jia_chen: meanwhile, can we check dedupe/curation issues? I suspect some prompts in goldlet were de-duplicated incorrectly during the recent fuzzyhash migration and that affected long-context anchors.
sara_morris: good call. @marc_d pull the original ingest hashes for the goldlet prompts and compare to the current promptset. look for any altered prompt prefixes.
marc_d: will do. also exporting the labeler annotations to a CSV for triage.
leila_ops: relabel workflow: please use this shorthand in the CSV: "REG" = regression, "FMT" = formatting-only, "OK" = acceptable. keep comments short.
sara_morris: for release decision: if regression ratio >5% on goldlet's longcode split we hold the kernel swap. otherwise can proceed with a mitigated rollout and increased monitoring.
tom_runtime: adding a short-circuit fallback rule to runtime: if average edit-distance regression > threshold on canary route, route to v1 automatically for 1m. pushing config now.
marc_d: evals done. preliminary: baseline accuracy 91.2, candidate 86.7 on longcode subset. full logs: https://redwood.infra/artifacts/1759876420/eval.json
jia_chen: that's >5% delta — looks like a real regression.
sara_morris: copy. leila, start the labeler switchover now and assemble a 200-example micro-gold expansion (add edge longcode + multistep dialog cases) so we have breath for future runs.
leila_ops: acknowledged. kicking off reassign: 30 labelers, priority window 6h. creating task batch id=mg-1759-1.
labelbot: Batch created: mg-1759-1 (200 items). Labels expected in ~5h at current throughput.
marc_d: i'll open a short PR to pin the kernel until we complete the triage: infra/kernel/pin-q4b-int8-v1 -> for canary routes.
sara_morris: thumbs up. after labeler annotations land, we'll run the judgement script and decide rollback vs targeted fix (tokenizer vs kv-compact).
marc_d: quick diff showed most failures are related to off-by-one token shifts at function boundaries. that screams tokenizer normalization.
jia_chen: can we attempt a token-normalization shim on the candidate and re-eval before full rollback? less disruptive than reverting kernel.
tom_runtime: can test a shim in staging cluster in ~30m, cheap to try.
sara_morris: do it. keep me posted in this thread. once we have labeler judgments we can finalize. thanks all :eyes:
deploy-bot: canary route pinned to q4b-int8-v1 by marc_d (PR #1427).
